scope: All 523 source glossary definitions reviewed; rendered 524th dfn is nested alias moment of inertia, not an independent definition.
status: Original audit snapshot with current group decisions; see individual statuses and glossary-wording-decisions.md

groups.issue: Defined in 11.2 through the Hertz/EM-wave discussion and restricted to EM waves, though 5.2 already explicitly introduces the unit.
groups.recommendation: Make 5.2 the formal introduction; define Hz as inverse seconds for frequency of any periodic process. Link from 11.2.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Glossary is in 11.3, attached to the antenna application; 5.6 already explains standing waves in detail.
groups.recommendation: Move the formal glossary association to 5.6; fixed nodes describe the pattern, not absence of motion everywhere.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Three forms of the same concept, including a later incidental adjective in 11.3; current resonance definition names driving frequency but omits the enhanced response.
groups.recommendation: Use resonance as the canonical entry in 5.4; make verb/adjective forms aliases or links. Explain enhanced response near a natural frequency.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Glossary appears in 9.5 without a corresponding explicit vector-addition paragraph there; wording unnecessarily includes positions.
groups.recommendation: Introduce explicitly with vectors in 1.3 if vector addition is to be taught there; otherwise attach to the first actual worked addition. Do not merely move the glossary without adding instruction.
groups.status: Resolved: glossary entry removed; no additional vector-addition instruction. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: General quantities are glossary terms in the 11.3 EM-wave application.
groups.recommendation: Associate electric-field magnitude with 9.4 and magnetic-field magnitude with 10.5; distinguish the introductory B usage from the technical H meaning of magnetic field strength.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Defined through microwave heating in 11.5 rather than the earlier thermal-physics treatment.
groups.recommendation: Use thermal motion as the canonical term in Chapter 8, with an explicit microscopic explanation near temperature/ideal-gas discussion; retain thermal agitation as an alias.
groups.status: Resolved: redundant glossary and formal-term styling removed; thermal motion already explained in earlier energy and heat sections. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Glossary entry in 12.7 has no corresponding explanatory paragraph there; the local source reads as an inherited leftover.
groups.recommendation: Review whether the concept is actually taught in the current sequence. Either add a deliberate introduction in the wave/quantum-wave discussion or remove this orphan entry; do not choose a location solely from an incidental mention.
groups.status: Resolved: glossary entry removed. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: In 14.5 the prose means a nuclear transformation equation, but the glossary means the time-dependent radioactive decay law.
groups.recommendation: Split the senses: nuclear decay equation in 14.5 and radioactive decay law in 14.6, or rename the glossary entry and define each at its actual use.
groups.status: Resolved: decay equation glossary entry removed; ordinary discussion retained. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Formal entry is in 12.3 although the newly canonical gamma-ray definition in 11.4 already uses photon, and earlier radiation passages do too.
groups.recommendation: Decide whether to give a brief first definition in 11.4 with deeper treatment in 12.3, or deliberately mark the earlier use as a preview. Keep one canonical glossary entry.
groups.status: Resolved: retain formal photon definition in Section 12.3; Section 11.4 is an incidental mention. Existing source already follows this arrangement; no textbook edit needed.

groups.issue: Exact-string deduplication missed these synonymous entries. The later voltage definition also slips from a difference to potential.
groups.recommendation: Keep electric current in 9.8 and potential difference (voltage) in 9.6; make later forms links or explicit aliases, not independent definitions.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Singular/plural entries describe the same particle in 9.2 and 14.4.
groups.recommendation: Use one proton entry; early charge description can precede later nuclear/quark detail, with a cross-reference.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Same law appears as separate glossary entries in 2.4 and 4.2.
groups.recommendation: Retain Newton’s second law in 2.4 and link the momentum formulation in 4.2; qualify average versus instantaneous force.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Two entries describe the same quantity in 14.6.
groups.recommendation: Use activity (decay rate) as one definition, distinguishing expected activity from a finite observed count rate.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

terms: magnetic field strength (magnitude) produced by a long straight current-carrying wire
magnetic field strength at the center of a circular loop
magnetic field strength inside a solenoid
groups.issue: Several glossary headwords are equation labels or descriptions of calculations.
groups.recommendation: Consider moving these to equation summaries and leaving the conceptual headwords in the glossary. Preserve anchors and all exercise numbers.
groups.status: Resolved: glossary entries and formal-term styling removed; equations and explanations retained. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Circular or procedural entries contribute little beyond the corresponding concept/formula.
groups.recommendation: Review whether these deserve glossary entries; use explanatory equations or cross-references if not.
groups.status: Resolved: glossary entries and formal-term styling removed; equations and explanations retained. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Defined as supporting weight on a resting surface; excludes walls, moving contacts, and other normal forces.
groups.recommendation: Define the perpendicular component of a contact force at a surface; revise the introducing prose in 2.6 if it has the same restriction.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Uses distance to the point of application instead of distance to the line of action.
groups.recommendation: Correct in 6.3 to perpendicular distance from the axis/pivot to the force’s line of action; check accompanying diagram/prose.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Voltage drop is called loss of electrical power; Joule’s law is presented as P=IV.
groups.recommendation: In 9.11 define potential decrease and distinguish general electrical power P=IV from resistive heating P=I²R. Review the explicit Joule’s-law sentence in the source too.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Electromagnetism is defined as using current to make magnets, and the prose repeats that definition.
groups.recommendation: Define the broader electric/magnetic interaction framework in 9.1 or a deliberate introductory passage; reserve current-produced magnetism for the electromagnet example in 10.3.
groups.status: Resolved: electromagnet definition and glossary in 10.3; electromagnetism definition and glossary in 11.2. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Ampere’s-law entry describes summing field contributions, closer to Biot-Savart; Biot-Savart definition says only that a specific equation exists.
groups.recommendation: Give distinct qualitative statements in 10.8, with the magnetostatic scope of Ampere’s law and later Maxwell extension made clear.
groups.status: Applied: approved prose and glossary definitions, with stable linked Maxwell section title. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Cage is said to prevent charge penetrating its surface; equilibrium says all free charges stop moving.
groups.recommendation: Use electrostatic field shielding and absence of net macroscopic charge flow; microscopic motion continues. Keep in 9.7.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Absolute zero says all molecular motion ceases; temperature is circularly defined by thermometer reading.
groups.recommendation: Define temperature through thermal equilibrium/heat-flow direction at this level and avoid denying quantum zero-point motion. Keep in 8.2.
groups.status: Applied: approved temperature definition and simple absolute-zero wording, without quantum caveat. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Superposition only says waves arrive together; overtones are equated with integer multiples; interference definitions cover only limiting phase cases.
groups.recommendation: State addition of disturbances, distinguish overtones from harmonics, and distinguish partial from complete interference in 5.6.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: SI examples include litre without distinguishing its accepted non-SI status; base units are defined by measurement procedures rather than their role in the system.
groups.recommendation: Update the unit-system explanation and definitions together in 0.3, using SI base/derived terminology and examples.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Atomic mass is given as the sum of constituent masses, omitting binding; reaction energy is called created.
groups.recommendation: In 14.4 define the atom’s mass including binding effects; in 14.5 define energy released/absorbed from initial-final mass-energy difference.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Glossary still uses feel/do not feel the strong force, despite revised prose explaining composite hadrons and elementary leptons.
groups.recommendation: Synchronize with the approved 14.13 prose. The old definitions wrongly include quarks/gluons as hadrons and photons as leptons.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

terms: conservation of total electron family number
conservation of total muon family number
groups.issue: Definitions assign ±1 without identifying particle versus antiparticle and state unqualified family-number conservation.
groups.recommendation: Explain counting particles minus antiparticles; qualify family conservation in light of neutrino oscillations, consistent with the existing discussion. Introduce in 14.13 and align earlier beta-decay references.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Gauge boson includes all four forces without qualification; Feynman diagram is treated as a literal time-position graph limited to virtual-particle exchange.
groups.recommendation: Define the Standard Model gauge carriers and diagrams as representations of interaction contributions. Keep explicit caution that a diagram is not a literal trajectory plot. Review 14.12/14.13 prose together.
groups.status: Applied: approved Feynman-diagram and gauge-boson wording, including gauge field. Pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: QCD is nearly circular; electroweak definition is vague; GUT and string entries sound established rather than proposed.
groups.recommendation: Define scope clearly in 14.14: QCD describes strong interactions of quarks/gluons; distinguish established electroweak theory from proposed further unification and string frameworks.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Positron is defined by one production channel; electron-neutrino definition does not distinguish it from other neutral elementary particles.
groups.recommendation: Define identity and flavor in 14.5, then describe production examples. Retain antielectron only as an explicit alias.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Beta entry excludes positrons; radioactivity/decay emphasize emitted rays or particles too narrowly for electron capture; gamma decay says gamma particle.
groups.recommendation: Review the nuclear-decay family together in 14.2/14.5, including spontaneous transformation and photon emission.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Scintillators are called a method rather than materials; Geiger tube is identified by an audio output supplied by readout electronics.
groups.recommendation: Define the detector mechanisms in 14.3; separate scintillating material, tube, and associated electronics.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Breeding is restricted to plutonium production; criticality uses easily; supercriticality describes an outcome rather than neutron multiplication balance.
groups.recommendation: Define fissile-material production more generally and criticality through neutron balance in 14.10. Note that critical mass depends on geometry, composition, moderation and surroundings.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Wording can imply instrument error or ignorance; probability wave is too vague.
groups.recommendation: Clarify intrinsic quantum spreads versus measurement imperfections in 12.5; treat energy-time carefully rather than as an identical operator pair. Requires coordinated prose review.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Time dilation suggests a moving observer’s own time slows; proper time refers to one event rather than an interval; Doppler wording says radiation moves relative to observer.
groups.recommendation: Clarify comparison of clocks/event pairs and source-observer motion in 13.3/13.5; retain existing equations after checking assumptions.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Broad introductory definitions are familiar but under-specified or circular: quantity of matter, remain in motion, ability to do work, and change.
groups.recommendation: Review as a foundational-language batch. Prefer operational relationships without imposing advanced formalism; current introduction sections are generally appropriate.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Distance duplicates displacement magnitude; range says maximum; some definitions silently assume ideal projectiles or uniform circles.
groups.recommendation: State distance-between-points versus path length, actual projectile horizontal range, and radial acceleration/force scope. Keep in Chapter 1/2 introductions.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Deformation is just displacement; restoring force is described as opposing another force; static friction opposes motion despite no slipping.
groups.recommendation: Describe change of shape/size, return toward equilibrium, stiffness, and opposition to impending relative slipping in 2.7/2.8.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Definitions can imply electrical energy requires current, bond breaking releases energy by itself, or thermal energy is only kinetic.
groups.recommendation: Coordinate energy-form definitions in 3.5 with the microscopic treatment in Chapter 8. Preserve the distinction between energy stored and energy transferred.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Pressure wording is awkward; buoyancy scope is not stated; Bernoulli relation is said to hold through the fluid without streamline/flow qualifications.
groups.recommendation: Clarify normal force per area, hydrostatic context and the steady ideal-flow assumptions in Chapter 7.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Mass normalization and conditions are unclear; isobaric wrongly requires work; reversible definition is confined to heat engines.
groups.recommendation: Clarify specific quantities and process conditions at their present Chapter 8 introductions.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Disorder is offered as the principal conceptual association and energy available for work is underspecified.
groups.recommendation: Review 8.13 and 8.14 together; use thermodynamic definition first and statistical interpretation later. This is an editorial choice requiring more than a glossary-only swap.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Field is restricted to a force map; point/test charge definitions rely on arbitrary symbol names; charge conservation is reduced to pair creation; electron implies a classical orbit.
groups.recommendation: Improve in place in 9.2/9.4, with a small/nonperturbing test charge and charge conservation for isolated systems; avoid literal electron orbits.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Curie entry implies no induced magnetization above the transition; μ0 is presented as exact; Lenz wording assigns opposition to voltage; AC is equated with sinusoidal behavior.
groups.recommendation: Clarify loss of spontaneous ferromagnetism, approximate numerical μ0, induced-current field direction, and sinusoidal AC as the case studied.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Definitions lean on one demonstration or geometry; image definitions omit ray convergence/backward extension.
groups.recommendation: In Chapter 11 distinguish frequency-dependent refractive behavior, paraxial focal geometry and actual/apparent ray origins. Qualify lens shape by surrounding refractive index.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Adjacent definitions still assume linear polarization although the new polarized-light entry allows more general polarization.
groups.recommendation: Review 11.11 as a coherent group; explicitly limit directional-plane language to linearly polarized light.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Some are historical descriptions instead of definitions; planetary model says only most familiar; Bohr radius says mean orbit radius; hydrogen wavelengths are restricted to visible light.
groups.recommendation: Clarify at current introductions, with model scope and minimum electron-removal energy. Keep distinctions between quantum states and literal classical orbits.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Several are vague, grammatical, or use an example as the definition. Curie is historically tied to radium rather than first stating the defined conversion.
groups.recommendation: Define quantities/objects directly in Chapter 14; decay constant as decay probability rate, radiopharmaceutical as radioactive diagnostic/therapeutic preparation, fission fragments as resulting nuclei. Check local prose alongside each.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Fusion gain has multiple boundaries; ignition lacks self-heating explanation; confinement is limited to lasers; cycle is only a list of reactions without multiplicities/net result.
groups.recommendation: Review together in 14.9, stating the intended gain measure and physical mechanism. Preserve equations but add conceptual definition where needed.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Definitions lean on historical nucleon counting and unqualified conservation.
groups.recommendation: Keep historical operational introduction, then add quark-count interpretation after quarks; match the agreed staged treatment of mesons/baryons.
groups.status: Applied: focused glossary and prose corrections; pending preview refresh.

groups.issue: Some entries are general vocabulary, detailed applications, or a restricted example presented as a general term.
groups.recommendation: Maintainer decision: retain only if useful to learning objectives; otherwise explain locally without creating a formal glossary headword. No automatic deletions recommended.
groups.status: Applied: maintainer-approved simplified wording and coordinated prose; G49 definitions only; pending preview refresh.
